atoms.b: The ancient Greeks valued beauty and decorated themselves with ((++bright boring)) colours and jewellery.
To them, beauty also meant being strong and ((++healthy ill)). You can see this in their art, which often shows young, ((++athletic weak)) bodies.

trainers.instruction: Select the item of clothing that is being described.

atoms.a: Men and women wore a cloak called a himation, using lighter fabric in summer and thicker material in winter.
A linen or cotton tunic called a chiton was usually worn underneath the himation
Some people wore leather sandals, but many walked around barefoot!
Gold wreath crowns were usually for royalty, but other jewellery was worn by the rich and the poor alike.

instruction.text: Match the jewellery material to the group that traditionally wore it in ancient Greece.

atoms.sound: Rich people wore gold and silver jewellery.
Poor people were bronze and pottery jewellery.

feedback.finish: People in ancient Greece were often buried with their jewellery, which has helped archaeologists learn about their social status, beliefs and daily life.

atoms.b: Both men and women cared for their skin, using olive ((++oil pits)) as a natural moisturiser.
Women used crushed ((++berries bones)) to colour their cheeks and lips and coal as eyeliner.

Pale skin was seen as a sign of ((++wealth bravery)), showing that a woman didn’t need to work outside. To achieve this look, many used lead powder to ((++whiten darken)) their skin without knowing that it is toxic!
